cases.translation: Every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
cases.explain: Семья is the grammatical subject of несчастлива, so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: С другой ___ крепко обнял подушку и прижался к ней щекой.
cases.translation: On the other side he tightly hugged the pillow and pressed his cheek to it.
cases.explain: In the idiom «с другой стороны» the preposition с governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Он не сумел приготовить свое лицо к тому ___, в которое он становился пред женой после открытия его вины.
cases.translation: He had not managed to prepare his face for the position he found himself in before his wife after the discovery of his guilt.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Увидав эту ___, Долли вздрогнула, как от физической боли, разразилась потоком жестоких слов и выбежала из комнаты.
cases.translation: Seeing this smile, Dolly shuddered as if from physical pain, burst into a stream of cruel words, and ran out of the room.
cases.explain: Улыбку is the direct object of the transitive verb увидав (seeing), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Разразилась со свойственной ей горячностью ___ жестоких слов и выбежала из комнаты.
cases.translation: She burst out, with her characteristic vehemence, in a stream of cruel words and ran out of the room.
cases.explain: The verb разразиться (to burst out) governs the instrumental case for the thing produced.

cases.sentence: Проснулся не в спальне жены, а в своем кабинете на софьянном ___.
cases.translation: He woke not in his wife's bedroom but in his study on the morocco-leather sofa.
cases.explain: The preposition на indicating location governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: К удивлению, не нашел ___ и в кабинете.
cases.translation: To his surprise, he did not find his wife in the study either.
cases.explain: The negated verb не нашел (did not find) takes its object in the genitive case (genitive of negation).

cases.sentence: Англичанка поссорилась с экономкой и написала записку ___, прося приискать ей новое место.
cases.translation: The English governess quarreled with the housekeeper and wrote a note to her friend, asking her to find her a new position.
cases.explain: Приятельнице is the indirect object of написала (wrote to), so it stands in the dative case.

reading.ru: Все счастливые семьи похожи друг на друга.
reading.question: What does the opening line say about happy families?
reading.explain: The text states «Все счастливые семьи похожи друг на друга» — all happy families resemble one another.

reading.question: What is the state of affairs in the Oblonsky household?
reading.explain: «Все смешалось в доме Облонских» means everything was in a muddle in the Oblonsky household.

reading.ru: Жена узнала, что муж был в связи с бывшую в их доме француженкую гувернанткой и объявила мужу, что не может жить с ним в одном доме.
reading.question: What did the wife discover about her husband?
options: He had an affair with the French governess
He was planning to travel abroad
reading.correct: He had an affair with the French governess
reading.explain: The text says the wife learned her husband had been involved with the French governess who had been in their house.

reading.ru: Дети бегали по всему дому, как потерянные.
reading.question: How did the children behave amid the household crisis?
options: They ran around the house like lost souls
They stayed quietly in their room
They went off to school as usual
reading.correct: They ran around the house like lost souls
reading.explain: «Дети бегали по всему дому, как потерянные» — the children ran about the house like lost creatures.

reading.ru: Повар ушел еще вчера со двора во время самого обеда.
reading.question: What did the cook do?
options: He left the household in the middle of dinner the day before
He was fired by the wife
reading.correct: He left the household in the middle of dinner the day before
reading.explain: The text states the cook had left the premises the day before, right in the middle of dinner.

reading.ru: На третий день после ссоры князь Степан Аркадьевич Облонский, Стива, как его звали в свете, в обычный час, то есть в восемь часов утра, проснулся не в спальне жены, а в своем кабинете на софьянном диване.
reading.question: Where did Stepan Arkadyich wake up on the third day after the quarrel?
options: In his study on the morocco-leather sofa
reading.correct: In his study on the morocco-leather sofa
reading.explain: The text says he woke not in his wife's bedroom but in his study on the morocco-leather divan.

reading.ru: «Да, да, как это было!» — думал он, вспоминая сон.
reading.question: What was Stepan Arkadyich doing as he woke?
reading.explain: He thought «Да, да, как это было!», trying to remember his dream.

reading.ru: Улыбка исчезла с его лица, он сморщил лоб.
reading.question: What happened to his smile when he remembered the quarrel?
reading.explain: «Улыбка исчезла с его лица, он сморщил лоб» — his smile disappeared and he wrinkled his brow.

reading.ru: Неприятнее всего была та первая минута, когда он, вернувшись из театра, веселым и довольным, с огромной грушей для жены в руке, не нашел жены в гостиной.
reading.question: What was he holding when he came home from the theater?
options: A large pear for his wife
reading.correct: A large pear for his wife
reading.explain: The text describes him returning from the theater with a huge pear for his wife in hand.

reading.ru: Увидав эту улыбку, Долли вздрогнула, как от физической боли, разразилась со свойственной ей горячностью потоком жестоких слов и выбежала из комнаты.
reading.question: How did Dolly react upon seeing his smile?
options: She shuddered, burst into a torrent of cruel words, and ran out of the room
reading.correct: She shuddered, burst into a torrent of cruel words, and ran out of the room
reading.explain: The text describes Dolly shuddering as from physical pain and bursting into a stream of harsh words before fleeing the room.
